qc.label_under_test: A year of the 1880s or 1890s written in digits, in any language (peaks on the decade digit: 18|8|x, 18|9|x, and '1890s'); years 1900-1909 fire about half as strongly, fading toward the end of that decade (1907-1909 about 0.1-0.2); years of the 1870s are in between (about 0.13-0.47, on the 7: often above 0.3, so they are neither clean fires nor clean misses); years before 1870 (including the 1850s-1860s, this neuron's other pole), the 1910s-1990s, 2000-2079 and earlier centuries stay quiet (under about 0.1); future years 2080-2099 used as years fire weakly (about 0.2-0.35); 1880s-1890s years spelled out in words fire weakly (about 0.1-0.3) and short forms like '89 stay quiet; late-19th-century era words with no 188x/189x digits (Gilded Age, fin de siecle) stay quiet. A bare four-digit 188x/189x code or ID that could be read as a year (a PIN, password, locker code, serial or phone-number ending) fires about 0.3-0.45 even in a modern setting, while a 188x/189x count, distance, price, route or apartment number is weak in a modern or neutral setting (about 0.02-0.2) but fires (about 0.2-0.6) when the text is set in the late 19th century, either through an earlier 1880s-1890s year or through a period cue such as the Gilded Age, the Wild West or Victorian England; after an earlier 1850s-1870s year it is unreliable (sometimes strong, up to about 0.8); written with a thousands comma (1,89x) it reaches about 0.2-0.4 in any setting
